extracted_fields.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Model-centric MoE serving analysis applied to a future wafer-scale GPU with multi-chiplet/HBM data placement and to an existing multi-GPU system including an 8xH100 case; simulator validation, architectural assumptions, interconnect, memory, power/area model and cluster configuration require per-experiment extraction.
extracted_fields.workload_or_design_corpus: Four 2025 MoE models—DeepSeek V3 (671B), Llama4-Maverick-128E (402B), Qwen3-235B (235B) and Kimi K2 (1000B)—profiled over more than 24,000 requests spanning diverse tasks, topics and languages; traces exceed 150 GB and are publicly released. The paper reports temporal layer/token/prefill-decode and spatial single-expert/co-activation analyses.

limits: Full-paper extraction from author preprint plus released trace-dataset reference; simulator calibration, exact request/model sampling, trace representativeness, wafer-scale architecture validity, baseline parity, tail/energy/cost results and transfer across routing distributions, topologies and serving stacks remain unresolved.

title: Patterns Behind Chaos: Forecasting Data Movement for Efficient Large-Scale MoE LLM Inference

extracted_fields.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Ramulator2 simulation of a shared CPU/PIM memory system modeled on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 888 host with 32GB DRAM; LPDDR5-6400, 2 channels x 2 ranks, 8GB/rank, 16 PIM units per rank, 1GHz PIM units with 6.4GB/s bandwidth and 1kB transfer buffers. DRAM energy uses DRAMPower; memory-controller area is synthesized with Synopsys Design Compiler using a TSMC 90nm library at 2.4GHz and scaled to a 5nm estimate. This is simulated/model-based evidence, not a measured phone implementation.
extracted_fields.workload_or_design_corpus: Three approximately billion-parameter LLMs—BLOOM-1B1, DeepSeek-R1-1.5B and Qwen2-0.5B—with 16-bit inputs and 8-bit weights; six mobile-app traces collected from a Xiaomi Mi 11 Pro, three PolyBench benchmarks and three SPEC CPU2017 benchmarks. COSM uses PEQ and PRWQ sizes of 2 per bank and a 128-cycle PIM execution command; baselines are All-Bank Command, Chopim, Chopim(128) and AsyncDIMM-Bank.

limits: Author-preprint extraction; headline results vary by context (abstract up to 2.8x and <2.0% CPU loss; introduction 2.6x and <2.2%), and energy excludes CPU-access energy. Simulator calibration, trace representativeness, artifact execution, implementation feasibility, thermal behavior and transfer beyond the modeled LPDDR5/Snapdragon setting remain unresolved.
title: COSM: A Cooperative Scheduling Framework for Concurrent PIM and CPU Execution on Mobile Devices

extracted_fields.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Cerberus targets single-device-per-channel HBM/LPDDR-style memory with on-die, link and system ECC. Reliability is evaluated by Monte Carlo error injection; performance uses Accel-Sim with an NVIDIA V100 model, 32 HBM channels and HBM4 at 6.4Gbps, while ECC latency/area uses synthesized logic (UMC 28nm) and HBM2E current-based energy estimates. No fabricated memory or GPU measurement is established.
extracted_fields.workload_or_design_corpus: Sixteen GPU workloads from Rodinia, Parboil, GraphBIG and PolyBench; fault scenarios cover in-bank SE/16E/32E/SE+SE, write-link SE/DQE/DQSE and out-of-bank SE/DE/DQE/DQSE, including multi-location combinations. Cerberus 32b/40b is compared with HBM4, Unity ECC and DUO under matched redundancy configurations.

limits: Full-preprint extraction; fault distributions are derived from cited studies rather than field remeasurement, GPU behavior is simulated, energy uses HBM2E currents and transfer-split assumptions, and area is normalized from UMC 28nm synthesis. The 33.3% redundancy, reliability, 0.7% IPC and energy claims require independent review and sensitivity to fault models, HBM generation, timing assumptions and code construction.

title: Cerberus: Cross-Layer ECC Co-Design for Robust and Efficient Memory Protection

extracted_fields.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Cassandra is evaluated with a PyTorch/custom-CUDA software emulator, Accel-Sim GPU modeling based on RTX 4090-like and Jetson AGX Orin systems, and a Scale-Sim/LPU cycle-level NPU model with a 64 TFLOPS MAC unit, 273 GB/s bandwidth and 128GB LPDDR5X. Encoder/decoder and a 64TFLOPS NPU with 9MB scratchpad are synthesized in Synopsys Design Compiler at 28nm, with Samsung 28nm SRAM Compiler area; GPU/NPU results are modeled, not measured commercial-device performance.
extracted_fields.workload_or_design_corpus: Reasoning LLM evaluation uses DeepSeek-R1-Distillated-Llama3-8B, Qwen3-8B-Thinking and Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 across AIME2025, Math-500, GPQA-Diamond, LongBench-QMSum and LiveCodeBench; GPQA-Diamond and Math-500 use 100-question samples while AIME2025 uses all questions. Performance uses four scenarios, 40% pruning, 4-bit weight and KV-cache truncation, and draft length gamma 3-5; baselines include BF16, SmoothQuant/W8A8, Draft&Verify, MagicDec, Lookahead Decoding and Eagle-3.

limits: Full author-preprint extraction; RTX 4090 results use Ampere traces because Accel-Sim lacks Ada-Lovelace support, NPU/GPU outcomes are simulated, the 2% area statement is for the modeled 64TFLOPS NPU, and acceptance/accuracy depend on model, task and compression settings. Calibration is about 128 samples for Wanda pruning and an 8-sample development grid search; reproduction, broader batch/device coverage, and independent review remain open.
source_locators: Sections VI-A to VI-D; Tables III-V
title: Cassandra: Enabling Reasoning LLMs at Edge via Self-Speculative Decoding

extracted_fields.hardware_or_process_assumptions: DisDP fully disaggregates compute, network and optimizer storage using one FPGA-based SmartNIC per GPU, a programmable SmartSwitch and one non-colocated parameter server. The prototype uses Xilinx U50 FPGA SmartNICs, eight 1xA100 GPU machines and one CPU machine under 100Gbps Ethernet; comparisons include ZeRO-Infinity, ZeRO-3, ATP and ZeRO-Offload, including an 8xA100 cluster with 600GB/s NVLink. The 32-GPU cost study uses ASTRA-sim throughput simulation and public component quotes, so its throughput-per-dollar result is not a measured 32-GPU deployment.
extracted_fields.workload_or_design_corpus: Model-sharded data-parallel LLM training with Custom-175B, OPT-1.3B, OPT-30B, OPT-66B and larger modeled sizes through 1T; experiments vary worker count, micro-batch size and network conditions. Reported end-to-end measurements use eight distributed GPUs, including 175B throughput/MFU and 66B fine-tuning on the rm-static dataset; convergence compares DisDP and ZeRO-Infinity in bf16. Maximum-size, scaling, faster-network and 32-GPU cost studies include modeled configurations.

limits: Full author-preprint extraction; the 8-GPU prototype results do not establish deployment-scale behavior for the modeled 32-GPU and 1T cases. SmartNIC/SmartSwitch resource tables, U50 DMA limitations, network topology, optimizer and storage costs, baseline tuning, simulator calibration, public-price assumptions, failure behavior, training-quality equivalence beyond the reported OPT-66B run and independent reproduction remain open. The paper also reports a 28% NCCL bandwidth advantage over DisDP on two GPUs without concurrent GEMM, showing that the benefit depends on concurrency, GPU count and SmartNIC DMA capability.
source_locators: Sections III-A to III-D; Tables II, VI-VII
Sections IV-F to IV-I; Tables VIII-IX
title: DisDP: Disaggregating Compute, Network, and Storage for Model-Sharded Data-Parallel Training
